convoLines.text: "What do you miss most? From before."
"Why do you ask? God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"Still on what you miss most. Forget it."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? That is all."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"Okay." Ellis looks down. "Okay. It was me. 1× Stone — I was hungry and I... I'm sorry." Their voice is small.
You don't answer. The quiet turns pointed.
The air goes tight. Their eyes narrow, just slightly.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"Can we talk? Have you seen anyone on the roads? Anyone at all? I'm asking everyone."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here? No pressure, though."
"I hear you. But don't let the fear eat the good parts. They're real, even when they're rare."
"Still on the kindest thing someone's done for you."
"What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Curious, is all. Sorry — forget I asked." They let it go, easy.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Be kind to yourself, okay?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I dreamed Aidan was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Good — the most useful thing you've learned, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Tanisha: "You. Yeah, you. What do you make of this?"
"Take your time."
"When's the last time you really laughed? Just... be straight with me."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on the last time you laughed. That's the priority."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Aidan always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'They fill the quiet. Anyway — where was I?' We still owe the last time you laughed a proper ending, too. No time to waste."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Jerusalem Artichoke — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Maybe not. But it's honest. I'll take honest."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — Wheel of Teeth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Same as always: we endure."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You asked why I wanted to know, about your first memory. Fair question. I'm still curious, if you ever feel like telling it."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up? You know?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Botros — Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You missed a real hot meal. Soup, you said — with a spoon. Any of that turn up?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Duel. They just... took Botros. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? At night I count the stars and name them after people."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask? Anyway, that's me."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Hannah — Hardened Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on what you did with your hands."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Hardened Duel. They just... took Hannah. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
